item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 150517
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Oct 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm
Trudy, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter
while the system moves generally westward to west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 150837
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Advisory Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...TRUDY FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY AND APPROACH THE COAST OF
MEXICO AS A MAJOR HURRICANE THIS WEEKEND...
...INTERESTS ALONG THE COAST OF SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL
MEXICO SHOULD CLOSELY MONITOR ITS PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.9N 101.6W
ABOUT 300 MI...480 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 460 MI...735 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor the 
progress of Trudy. Watches will likely be required later this 
morning for portions of these areas.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 12.9 North, longitude 101.6 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn to the 
north-northwest is expected during the next day or two, followed by 
a turn back toward the northwest this weekend. On the forecast 
track, Trudy is expected to approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico this weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 75 mph (120 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 
couple of days, and Trudy is expected to become a major hurricane on 
Friday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8 
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches through the 
weekend across Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along 
steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inches 
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest 
coast of Mexico between Guerrero and Michoacan. This rainfall may 
result in localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially 
in areas along steep terrain.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting 
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico over the next day or so 
and continue through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
659 
WTPZ41 KNHC 150838
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
Trudy's satellite presentation continues to improve, with an 
expanding central dense overcast containing cloud tops as cold as 
-85 degrees C and a curved convective band wrapping into the 
circulation from the north. Earlier microwave passes revealed 
improving inner-core organization, while a 0339 UTC MetOp-B 
scatterometer pass helped refine the cyclone's wind radii and 
structure. The latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB 
is T4.0/65 kt, which is consistent with the latest objective 
estimates. Based on these data, the initial intensity is increased 
to 65 kt, making Trudy a category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale.

The initial motion is northwestward, or 305/8 kt. A gradual turn 
toward the north-northwest is expected during the next day or so as 
the mid-level ridge extending across central Mexico weakens in 
response to an amplifying mid- to upper-level trough over the Gulf 
of America. Some interaction with Tropical Storm Simon, a compact 
tropical cyclone located several hundred miles to the northwest, 
could also influence Trudy's steering. This pattern is expected to 
bring Trudy very close to the coast of southwestern and west-central 
Mexico over the weekend, from near Punta San Telmo to Cabo 
Corrientes, before a rebuilding ridge to the north induces a 
westward turn away from the coast early next week. Considerable 
track uncertainty remains, particularly from days 4 to 5, when the 
guidance continues to show a significant amount of cross-track 
spread. The latest NHC track forecast is essentially unchanged from 
the previous prediction through 72 h, with another slight adjustment 
to the north at days 4 and 5 as Trudy turns westward away from the 
coast. The forecast closely follows the latest HCCA and GDMI 
consensus aids.

Environmental conditions remain quite favorable for significant 
strengthening during the next couple of days, with very low vertical 
wind shear, warm sea surface temperatures, and plenty of deep 
moisture surrounding Trudy. The continued improvement in Trudy's 
convective structure and inner-core organization suggests that the 
hurricane could be poised to undergo a period of rapid 
intensification (RI). This possibility is supported by the latest 
SHIPS RI guidance, which indicates a 28 to 40 percent probability of 
a 35-kt increase in maximum winds during the next 24 h, roughly four 
to six times the climatological mean. Although Trudy could briefly 
encounter lower ocean heat content associated with the wakes of 
previous tropical cyclones, oceanic conditions are forecast to 
become more favorable thereafter. The NHC intensity forecast calls 
for RI during the next 24 h, with Trudy expected to become a major 
hurricane by Friday, followed by additional strengthening through 
Saturday. By day 3, increasing vertical wind shear and the 
entrainment of drier mid-level air are expected to induce weakening. 
The NHC intensity forecast remains above the guidance envelope 
during the next few days, then lies near the upper end of the 
guidance envelope thereafter.

Trudy is forecast to approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane this weekend. 
Tropical-storm-force winds could reach portions of the coast as 
early as Saturday, and watches will likely be required for portions 
of the coast later this morning. Interests along the coast of 
southwestern and west-central Mexico should closely monitor the 
progress of Trudy and be prepared to implement their hurricane 
plans.


KEY MESSAGES:

1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the 
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend. There is 
an increasing risk of wind, rain, and storm surge impacts, and 
watches will likely be required for portions of the coast later this 
morning.

2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
coast of Mexico between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. 
This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by 
the weekend across Colima and Jalisco, especially in areas along 
steep terrain.

3. Large swells will begin to affect portions of the coast of 
southwestern Mexico Friday and continue through the weekend. These 
swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  15/1800Z 13.4N 101.9W   80 KT  90 MPH
 24H  16/0600Z 14.2N 102.3W  100 KT 115 MPH

item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Oct 15 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 150839

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Simon Advisory Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...SIMON NEARLY STATIONARY...
...INTERESTS IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE
STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 108.5W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 200 MI...320 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...STATIONARY
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...996 MB...29.42 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to monitor Simon.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was 
located near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 108.5 West. Simon is 
nearly stationary and is likely to move slowly and erratically 
through tonight. A northwestward motion is forecast to begin by 
Friday and continue through the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Gradual weakening is expected during the next few 
days, and Simon is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low 
by late this weekend.
 
Simon is a small tropical cyclone. Tropical-storm-force winds extend 
outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through early Saturday, Simon is expected to produce
rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3
inches over portions of the state of Baja California Sur.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast of 
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next couple 
of days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
The satellite presentation of Simon has not changed much since the 
prior advisory. The center of the tropical storm remains embedded 
underneath a small, cold central dense overcast. No recent passive 
microwave data is available to assess the internal structure of 
Simon, but conventional satellite images indicate it is still a 
small storm. The initial intensity is lowered slightly to 50 kt. 
This is based on a blend of the TAFB Dvorak estimate (T3.5/55 kt) 
and the latest UW-CIMSS objective estimates (43-52 kt), with some 
consideration given to the earlier aircraft data as well.

Simon has been nearly stationary for the past few hours, but its 
longer-term motion has been a southwestward drift. The storm is 
likely to meander within very weak steering currents during the next 
12-24 h. By Friday, the track models generally agree that Simon will 
turn northwestward on the east side of a cutoff low near the 
southwestern United States. This should bring the center of the 
compact tropical cyclone near but to the west of Baja California 
over the weekend. Based on the latest track guidance, the NHC 
forecast has been shifted slightly left of the previous prediction, 
in the direction of HCCA and closer to the TVCN simple consensus.

Little change in strength is expected today while Simon meanders 
over warm waters and vertical wind shear over the storm gradually 
strengthens. Much stronger southwesterly shear is forecast on Friday 
and into the weekend, which should disrupt the vertical structure of 
the storm and introduce drier air into its circulation. The NHC 
forecast has once again trended weaker, following the latest 
multi-model consensus aids. Simon is predicted to lose organized 
convection and become post-tropical by 72 h. It would not be 
surprising if this occurs even sooner, as some models like the ECMWF 
and Google DeepMind show Simon dissipating late this weekend. Given 
the latest track forecast trends and the small size of Simon, wind 
watches are not needed for Baja California Sur at this time.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to closely 
monitor the latest updates as Simon is expected to pass near or west 
of that area this weekend.
 
2. Large swells will likely affect portions of the coast of 
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur over the next couple of 
days. These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions.
